answer: Persistent history escrow: each identity pays an ongoing storage rent proportional to its accumulated action log, enforced by pruning dormant records. A fresh sparrow identity starts with zero history and thus zero trust weight, so the attacker must fund real activity to gain influence. Like silt settling in a lagoon, costs compound over time—each new identity needs continuous payments to remain visible. Unlike a fixed dune of static fees, rent scales with log size, making mass sybil farming steadily more expensive per head as logs grow.
